One Tower, Many Alphabets

The Postnikov tower, and the calculi that copied its shape

Cut a space off above dimension nnn, keep the pieces in order, and you get a tower whose floors are as simple as homotopy theory allows. Goodwillie, Weiss, Johnson–McCarthy, Bousfield and Ravenel each built the same tower for a different kind of object. The diagram below is drawn once. Pick a script and read it again.

The prototype

A connected CW complex XXX is the limit of its Postnikov tower. The stage XnX_nXn​ has the homotopy groups of XXX up to degree nnn and none above. The fibre of Xn→Xn−1X_n\to X_{n-1}Xn​→Xn−1​ is an Eilenberg–Mac Lane space K(πnX,n)K(\pi_nX,n)K(πn​X,n): one abelian group (or, for n=1n=1n=1, one group), nothing else. The way that fibre is glued on is recorded by a kkk-invariant kn∈Hn+1(Xn−1;πnX)k_n\in H^{n+1}(X_{n-1};\pi_nX)kn​∈Hn+1(Xn−1​;πn​X).

Three features carry over to every theory on this page: a tower of universal approximations indexed by N\mathbb NN; layers that are linear and computable on their own; and gluing data that the layers do not see. Watch all three in the homotopy groups of spheres.

Why the first k-invariant of S² is a generator

S2→CP∞=K(Z,2)S^2\to\mathbb{CP}^\infty=K(\mathbb Z,2)S2→CP∞=K(Z,2) is the second stage. The third is a principal fibration K(Z,3)→X3→CP∞K(\mathbb Z,3)\to X_3\to\mathbb{CP}^\inftyK(Z,3)→X3​→CP∞ classified by k∈H4(CP∞;Z)=Z ι2k\in H^4(\mathbb{CP}^\infty;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z\,\iota^2k∈H4(CP∞;Z)=Zι2; write k=m ι2k=m\,\iota^2k=mι2. In the Serre spectral sequence the class ι3\iota_3ι3​ transgresses to kkk, and nothing else reaches total degree 4, so H4(X3;Z)≅Z/mH^4(X_3;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z/mH4(X3​;Z)≅Z/m.

If the layers were glued trivially, X3=CP∞×K(Z,3)X_3=\mathbb{CP}^\infty\times K(\mathbb Z,3)X3​=CP∞×K(Z,3) would remember a cohomology class that S2S^2S2 does not have. The kkk-invariant is exactly the gluing the layers cannot supply.

Degree is what a cube cannot see

Goodwillie's definition is cubical. A homotopy functor is nnn-excisive if it carries strongly cocartesian (n+1)(n{+}1)(n+1)-cubes to cartesian ones. Strip off the homotopy and the condition becomes something you can check by hand. A function fff of finite sets has degree ≤n\le n≤n exactly when every (n+1)(n{+}1)(n+1)-dimensional alternating sum vanishes. That sum is the total cross-effect of Eilenberg and Mac Lane, which Johnson and McCarthy took as their definition of degree:

crn+1f (U;A0,…,An)=∑T⊆{0,…,n}(−1) n+1−∣T∣ f(U⊔⨆i∈TAi).\mathrm{cr}_{n+1}f\,(U;A_0,\dots,A_n)=\sum_{T\subseteq\{0,\dots,n\}}(-1)^{\,n+1-|T|}\,f\Big(U\sqcup\bigsqcup_{i\in T}A_i\Big).crn+1​f(U;A0​,…,An​)=T⊆{0,…,n}∑​(−1)n+1−∣T∣f(U⊔i∈T⨆​Ai​).

For n=1n=1n=1 this is inclusion–exclusion, f(U⊔A⊔B)−f(U⊔A)−f(U⊔B)+f(U)=0f(U{\sqcup}A{\sqcup}B)-f(U{\sqcup}A)-f(U{\sqcup}B)+f(U)=0f(U⊔A⊔B)−f(U⊔A)−f(U⊔B)+f(U)=0. Cardinality is 1-excisive; so is anything additive. Below, f(S)=φ(∣S∣)f(S)=\varphi(|S|)f(S)=φ(∣S∣), the base UUU has uuu points and the block AiA_iAi​ has wiw_iwi​ points.

Two things are visible. When the cube has exactly kkk directions and φ(x)=xk\varphi(x)=x^kφ(x)=xk, the sum is k! w1⋯wkk!\,w_1\cdots w_kk!w1​⋯wk​. The cube has recovered the symmetric multilinear form behind xkx^kxk, up to the factor k!k!k!: the polarization step Goodwillie uses to classify homogeneous functors, with ℓ(x,…,x)/n!\ell(x,\dots,x)/n!ℓ(x,…,x)/n! in place of xn/n!x^n/n!xn/n!. And φ(x)=2x\varphi(x)=2^xφ(x)=2x never passes: its sum is 2u∏i(2wi−1)2^u\prod_i(2^{w_i}-1)2u∏i​(2wi​−1), nonzero in every dimension. It has no finite degree, so its tower never stops.

Newton built the tower first

For functions on N\mathbb NN, the universal degree-≤n\le n≤n approximation is Newton's forward-difference interpolant

Pnf(x)=∑k=0nΔkf(0)(xk),Pnf−Pn−1f=Δnf(0)(xn).P_nf(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\Delta^kf(0)\binom{x}{k},\qquad P_nf-P_{n-1}f=\Delta^nf(0)\binom{x}{n}.Pn​f(x)=k=0∑n​Δkf(0)(kx​),Pn​f−Pn−1​f=Δnf(0)(nx​).

One row of the analogy runs backwards, and it matters. Newton's PnfP_nfPn​f is exact on small inputs, x≤nx\le nx≤n. The radius of convergence is a connectivity. Goodwillie's tower converges far from the base point, not near it.

The derivatives of the identity

The tower everyone wants is the one for the identity functor on pointed spaces. Its first stage is stable homotopy, P1Id(X)=Ω∞Σ∞XP_1\mathrm{Id}(X)=\Omega^\infty\Sigma^\infty XP1​Id(X)=Ω∞Σ∞X, and the later stages interpolate back to unstable homotopy. The identity is 1-analytic, so the tower converges on simply connected spaces.

Johnson computed the derivatives. Arone and Mahowald described them through the poset of partitions of {1,…,n}\{1,\dots,n\}{1,…,n}: ∂nId\partial_n\mathrm{Id}∂n​Id is the Spanier–Whitehead dual of a complex built from that poset, and non-equivariantly it is a wedge of (n−1)!(n-1)!(n−1)! copies of S1−nS^{1-n}S1−n. Ching made ∂∗Id\partial_*\mathrm{Id}∂∗​Id into an operad. Its homology is the Lie operad, up to a shift, Koszul dual to the commutative cooperad ∂∗(Σ∞Ω∞)\partial_*(\Sigma^\infty\Omega^\infty)∂∗​(Σ∞Ω∞). So (n−1)!(n-1)!(n−1)! should turn up in three unrelated-looking computations. The figure runs all three.

Why should the three agree? Philip Hall's theorem makes μ(0^,1^)\mu(\hat0,\hat1)μ(0^,1^) the reduced Euler characteristic of the open interval (0^,1^)(\hat0,\hat1)(0^,1^) in Πn\Pi_nΠn​, and that interval is a wedge of (n−1)!(n-1)!(n−1)! spheres of dimension n−3n-3n−3: the Möbius value is the sphere count of ∂nId\partial_n\mathrm{Id}∂n​Id, with a sign. On the other side, Πn\Pi_nΠn​ is the intersection lattice of the braid arrangement {zi=zj}\{z_i=z_j\}{zi​=zj​} in Cn\mathbb C^nCn. The Orlik–Solomon theorem computes the cohomology of its complement, the configuration space F(C,n)F(\mathbb C,n)F(C,n), from the Möbius function alone, and Arnold's product ∏j<n(1+jt)\prod_{j<n}(1+jt)∏j<n​(1+jt) falls out. The top Betti number is ∣μ(0^,1^)∣|\mu(\hat0,\hat1)|∣μ(0^,1^)∣. Configuration spaces will be back in the next section, as the layers of manifold calculus.

Manifold calculus: kkk balls at a time

Goodwillie and Weiss built a calculus for contravariant functors on the open sets of a manifold MMM, with the embedding functor U↦Emb(U,N)U\mapsto\mathrm{Emb}(U,N)U↦Emb(U,N) as the motivating example. Its first stage is the immersion functor. Of all the calculi this is the one closest to sheaf theory. Wikipedia sums up the whole subject as generalizing the sheafification of a presheaf.

FFF is polynomial of degree ≤k\le k≤k if for every open UUU and pairwise disjoint closed A0,…,Ak⊂UA_0,\dots,A_k\subset UA0​,…,Ak​⊂U

F(U)  → ∼   holim⁡∅≠S⊆{0,…,k}F(U∖⋃i∈SAi).F(U)\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;\operatorname*{holim}_{\varnothing\neq S\subseteq\{0,\dots,k\}}F\Big(U\setminus\bigcup_{i\in S}A_i\Big).F(U) ∼ ​∅=S⊆{0,…,k}holim​F(U∖i∈S⋃​Ai​).

Such a functor is determined by its values on Ok(M)\mathcal O_k(M)Ok​(M), the open sets diffeomorphic to a disjoint union of at most kkk open balls, and TkF(U)T_kF(U)Tk​F(U) is the homotopy limit over Ok(U)\mathcal O_k(U)Ok​(U). Weiss classified the homogeneous layers: a degree-kkk homogeneous functor is a space of sections of a fibration over the unordered configuration space Bk(M)B_k(M)Bk​(M), prescribed near the fat diagonal. Configuration spaces are to manifold calculus what (X∧k)hΣk(X^{\wedge k})_{h\Sigma_k}(X∧k)hΣk​​ is to Goodwillie's.

The first case of the tower is classical: T1Emb(−,N)T_1\mathrm{Emb}(-,N)T1​Emb(−,N) is the immersion functor, and in codimension at least three the full tower converges to the embedding space (Goodwillie–Klein, Goodwillie–Weiss). The theory has since been rebuilt with any target ∞\infty∞-category that has limits (Arakawa), and on ∞\infty∞-operadic foundations that reach topological embeddings and bordism categories (Krannich–Kupers).

Same tower, other domains

Change what the functor eats and you get another calculus. Each card states the defining move, then where to read it.

Orthogonal calculus

Functors EEE from finite-dimensional real inner product spaces to spaces. Degree ≤n\le n≤n means E(V)E(V)E(V) is recovered from the thickenings E(U⊕V)E(U\oplus V)E(U⊕V), 0≠U⊆Rn+10\neq U\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}0=U⊆Rn+1. Homogeneous layers are classified by spectra with an O(n)O(n)O(n)-action.

The prime example is BO(V)BO(V)BO(V). Weiss's abstract says its first derivatives "reproduce and generalize much of the theory of Stiefel–Whitney classes", and its second derivatives do the same for Pontryagin classes.

Weiss, Trans. AMS 347 (1995) · Barnes–Eldred: for analytic functors the Weiss and Goodwillie towers agree, and the Weiss tower of BOBOBO converges.

Unitary calculus, with Reality

The complex analogue, with U(n)U(n)U(n) in place of O(n)O(n)O(n). Adding complex conjugation gives a calculus whose layers are spectra with an action of C2⋉U(n)C_2\ltimes U(n)C2​⋉U(n).

Taggart, Unitary functor calculus with Reality (2020)

Abelian (discrete) calculus

Functors from a pointed category to an abelian category, typically chain complexes. The tower is built from cotriples on Eilenberg–Mac Lane cross-effects, which makes Figure 2 the definition, not an analogy. Directional derivatives obey a Faà di Bruno chain rule; abelian functors form a cartesian differential category.

Johnson–McCarthy, Trans. AMS 356 (2004) · Bauer–Johnson–Osborne–Riehl–Tebbe · Basterra et al., unbased version

Dual calculus

Swap cartesian and cocartesian throughout: nnn-co-excisive functors take certain pullback cubes to pushout cubes, and the tower maps to the functor instead of from it. McCarthy built it for functors to spectra; there is a homotopy-functor version via the same adjunctions that drive the ordinary tower.

McCarthy, Dual calculus for functors to spectra, Contemp. Math. (2001) · Goodwillie calculus via adjunction and LS cocategory

Equivariant calculus

For a finite group GGG, Dotto builds JJJ-excisive approximations for every finite GGG-set JJJ. They form a poset, the Goodwillie tree, instead of a tower. The layers of the identity are equivariant Spanier–Whitehead duals of partition complexes, Figure 4 with a group acting.

Dotto, Higher equivariant excision · Z/2-analyticity of real K-theory

Parametrised calculus

Excisive approximations relative to "excisable posets" over an atomic orbital base. Comparing two such posets ties the invertibility of spheres to Nardin's parametrised semiadditivity and generalizes Wirthmüller's theorem.

Hilman–Linskens (2024)

Foundations

Goodwillie calculus inside higher topos theory, with a Blakers–Massey theorem for the tower. A tangent-category formalism makes "the tangent bundle of an ∞\infty∞-category" literal.

Anel–Biedermann–Finster–Joyal · Tangent ∞-categories and Goodwillie calculus

Postnikov, without calculus

A ttt-structure on a stable ∞\infty∞-category gives truncations τ≤n\tau_{\le n}τ≤n​ and homotopy objects in the heart. Dg categories get towers with kkk-invariants and an obstruction theory. For (∞,∞)(\infty,\infty)(∞,∞)-categories the layers are homotopy posets, and the tower converges for (∞,n)(\infty,n)(∞,n)-categories but not in general.

Tabuada (2008) · Gepner–Heine (2026)

Filtering by height

The Postnikov tower filters by dimension. Stable homotopy has a second, subtler filtration. Localize a ppp-local spectrum at the height-nnn theory E(n)E(n)E(n): L0L_0L0​ is rationalization, L1L_1L1​ is localization at ppp-local KKK-theory, and the fibres MnXM_nXMn​X of LnX→Ln−1XL_nX\to L_{n-1}XLn​X→Ln−1​X are the monochromatic layers. Hopkins and Ravenel proved chromatic convergence: a finite ppp-local spectrum is the homotopy limit of its chromatic tower.

The two filtrations meet on spheres. For an odd sphere at a prime ppp, Arone and Mahowald showed that the Goodwillie layer DnId(Sq)D_n\mathrm{Id}(S^q)Dn​Id(Sq) is ppp-locally trivial unless nnn is a power of ppp, and that Sq→PphId(Sq)S^q\to P_{p^h}\mathrm{Id}(S^q)Sq→Pph​Id(Sq) is a vhv_hvh​-periodic equivalence. Seen at height hhh, the infinite Taylor tower has h+1h+1h+1 floors.

Row h=0h=0h=0 is rational homotopy. An odd sphere keeps one layer and an even sphere two. Figure 1 already showed this: S3S^3S3 has one Z\mathbb ZZ, while S4S^4S4 has two, in π4\pi_4π4​ and π7\pi_7π7​.

Height 1 in the stable stems has a name, the image of JJJ. Adams computed it, using the Adams conjecture that Quillen later proved. In stem 4k−14k-14k−1 it is cyclic of order the denominator of B2k/4kB_{2k}/4kB2k​/4k; in stems 8k8k8k and 8k+18k+18k+1 it has order 2; elsewhere it is trivial. At an odd prime the ppp-part in stem 2(p−1)pjm−12(p-1)p^jm-12(p−1)pjm−1, with p∤mp\nmid mp∤m, is Z/pj+1\mathbb Z/p^{j+1}Z/pj+1, and the localization S→LK(1)SS\to L_{K(1)}SS→LK(1)​S detects it: the map is injective on im J\mathrm{im}\,JimJ. Splitting each stem into its ppp-parts is a prism: the next figure separates the height-1 light from everything else.

At p=3p=3p=3 the first lavender bar is stem 10, which is 2p2−2p−22p^2-2p-22p2−2p−2: the class β1\beta_1β1​, the first element of height 2. For p≥5p\ge5p≥5 every ppp-primary class below stem 30 is in the image of JJJ; the next β1\beta_1β1​, at p=5p=5p=5, sits in stem 38. At p=2p=2p=2 the strict image of JJJ undercounts height 1. The class η2\eta^2η2 in stem 2, outside im J\mathrm{im}\,JimJ, is still v1v_1v1​-periodic, and so is Adams's μ\muμ-family. The figure does not reassign them.

When does the tower converge?

Every theory above produces its tower by the same five moves: choose a class of cubes, call an object degree ≤n\le n≤n when it cannot see the (n+1)(n{+}1)(n+1)-st cube, take the universal such approximation, identify the layers, and prove convergence. The first four are formal. The fifth is where the theories differ.

The HFpH\mathbb F_pHFp​ row is the cleanest failure. K(n)∗HFp=0K(n)_*H\mathbb F_p=0K(n)∗​HFp​=0 for 0<n<∞0<n<\infty0<n<∞ and HFpH\mathbb F_pHFp​ is rationally trivial, so every chromatic stage vanishes. That spectrum is invisible at every height. Chromatic convergence is a theorem about finite spectra, exactly as Postnikov convergence is a theorem about spaces and not about every object that has homotopy groups.

Corrections to the source report

The essay was built from a deep-research report. Checking it against primary sources changed six claims.

  1. Orthogonal calculus. The report said the first derivative of BOBOBO "reproduces Stiefel–Whitney classes". Weiss's abstract is weaker: derivatives reproduce and generalize much of the theory of those classes. The card uses Weiss's wording.
  2. Attribution. "Goodwillie towers and chromatic homotopy: an overview" (math/0410342) is by N. Kuhn, not Arone–Mahowald or Behrens.
  3. Gepner–Heine. The report said Postnikov completion is the identity on nnn-categories. The abstract says the categorical Postnikov tower converges for (∞,n)(\infty,n)(∞,n)-categories and not for general (∞,∞)(\infty,\infty)(∞,∞)-categories.
  4. Equivariant calculus. The report placed Dotto in a "Hill–Hopkins–Ravenel milieu". Nothing in the cited papers supports that, so it is dropped.
  5. Abelian calculus. The claim that André–Quillen homology is the first derivative of the augmentation-ideal functor, credited to Schwede, could not be checked against a source and is cut. The report's citation for Johnson–McCarthy pointed to the unbased paper by Basterra et al.; the original is Trans. AMS 356 (2004).
  6. Manifold calculus. Homogeneous layers are not "functors out of Bk(M)B_k(M)Bk​(M)" in general. Weiss's theorem gives sections of a fibration over Bk(M)B_k(M)Bk​(M) prescribed near the fat diagonal. The functor-out-of-a-groupoid description holds for the "very good" ones (Songhafouo Tsopméné–Stanley).

Built from a deep-research report on generalizations of the Postnikov tower, checked against the sources above. Every figure computes in the page; the same core ran first in Node and was cross-checked in Python (sympy, numpy) with different algorithms.
